newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-RILEY SHARES LEAD BEFORE STORM HALTS PLAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RILEY SHARES LEAD BEFORE STORM HALTS PLAY.

text.p: Australian Wayne Riley grabbed a
share of the first round lead with a six-under par 66 before a
gale forced play to be suspended at the Australian PGA
championship on Thursday.
Riley, who finished 16th on the European Tour money-winning
list this year, took full advantage on the benign early morning
conditions at the New South Wales course.
But tournament organisers had to halt play in mid-afternoon
when
strong winds began blowing balls off the greens as players
stood over their putts.
Riley, who fired four birdies and an eagle, shared the
lead with compatriot Bryan Roach. A group of four, including
Briton Ben Jackson were two shots further back in joint third
place.
In a bizarre incident, Australia's Mike Clayton suffered a
one stroke penalty after he inadvertently touched his ball after
a putt.
The problems began when Clayton, a regular on the European
Tour, threw his putter into the air in frustration after
narrowly missing a putt on the 14th green.
Realising the club might hit his ball, Clayton dived forward
in a failed attempt to catch his putter. A prostrate Clayton
could only look on in despair after his putter hit the ball on
the second bounce, his putter then knocking the ball against his
outstretched arm.
Clayton was only penalised one stroke under Rule 18 by
tournament officials because his ball had stopped moving.
"It flashed through my mind that if I didn't catch (the
putter), it would hit the ball," Clayton said.
"I just presumed it was two shots because I didn't think you
could do that many things wrong and get away with just one
shot," he said.
Clayton was two-over when play was stopped and will join
53 other players in completing their first rounds on Friday.
